about.intro_content: Prof. Yao-Jun Zhang is a Professor in the Department of Liver Surgery at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou. His clinical and research focus is locoregional and interventional therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
about.detailed_content: Prof. Zhang has co-authored numerous studies on liver cancer prognosis and treatment alongside SYSUCC's liver surgery team, including research on the impact of oral anti-hepatitis B therapy on survival in HCC patients treated with chemoembolisation, and studies on vascular patterns associated with HCC metastasis. He serves as an investigator on prospective liver cancer prognosis research at SYSUCC.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Yao-Jun Zhang

items.question: Does Prof. Yao-Jun Zhang accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to liver cancer at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Zhang's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Zhang specialises in locoregional and interventional therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma, including transarterial chemoembolisation.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Does Prof. Zhang treat hepatitis B-related liver cancer?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Zhang has researched the combined use of antiviral therapy and locoregional treatment such as chemoembolisation in patients with hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma.

items.question: Is Prof. Zhang involved in liver cancer research studies?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Zhang is an investigator on prospective liver cancer prognosis research at SYSUCC and has co-authored studies on HCC metastasis mechanisms.
